text:
ConocoPhillips dropped 0.6% today to $136.27, continuing a steep two-week decline of nearly 10% that began right after the company reported quarterly earnings on November 5th. The stock has fallen roughly $18 in that span, suggesting investors reacted negatively to the earnings results themselves or to forward guidance the company provided—though the specific details of that reaction aren't captured in the available news headlines.

The broader oil market remains a headwind: US crude is trading at $99.64 per barrel, down sharply from where it was two weeks ago when the stock was at $154. Even with global oil prices holding higher at $107, the weakness in domestic crude pricing limits upside for US-based producers. Geopolitical risk from stalled Iran negotiations could theoretically support energy prices, but that hasn't been enough to reverse the stock's momentum since earnings.
